cases.description: DOCUMENTS: design-doc draft, three dimensions in one request; good draft with a TBD testing section

request.state:
DRAFT DESIGN DOC
Title: Rate limiter for public API
Problem: Bursty clients cause p99 latency spikes on the orders API (measured 2.4s at peak on Sept 3).
Proposal: Token bucket per API key in Redis, 100 req/s sustained, burst 200. Return 429 with Retry-After. Fallback to local in-memory limiter if Redis is down (fail open, alert on-call).
Alternatives considered: sliding window log (rejected: memory heavy), gateway-level limiting (rejected: no per-key data).
Testing: TBD.
Rollout: TBD.

clarity.instructions: Rate how clearly the problem and proposal are stated.

alternatives.instructions: Rate how well alternatives and tradeoffs are covered.
criteria: several alternatives with explicit rejection reasons

testing_plan.instructions: Rate how complete the testing plan section is.
criteria: detailed plan with unit, load and failure-injection tests

cases.description: DOCUMENTS: complete incident postmortem; impact, root cause and action items all specific, scores high

request.state:
POSTMORTEM
Incident: checkout outage on Sept 12, 41 minutes, 8% of orders failed (about 3,100 orders, $190k GMV delayed).
Root cause: a config push lowered the DB connection pool from 200 to 20; pool exhaustion caused timeouts. The canary did not catch it because canary traffic was 1%.
Timeline: 14:02 push, 14:09 alert, 14:31 rollback decision, 14:43 recovered.
Action items: (1) block pool-size changes below 50% of current without review - owner Dev Patel, due Sept 26. (2) raise canary traffic to 10% for config pushes - owner Lin Zhao, due Oct 3. (3) add pool-saturation alert at 80% - owner Dev Patel, due Sept 22.

impact.instructions: Rate how well the impact is quantified.
criteria: quantified in duration, share of users and business cost

root_cause.instructions: Rate how specific and evidenced the root cause is.
criteria: specific mechanism and why it was not caught earlier

action_items.instructions: Rate how actionable the follow-up items are.
criteria: some items missing owners or dates
every item has an owner and a due date

RUNBOOK: Restarting the payments consumer
1. Run `kubectl -n payments get pods -l app=consumer` and confirm at least one pod is CrashLoopBackOff.
2. Run `kubectl -n payments rollout restart deploy/consumer`; wait until `rollout status` reports success (usually 90 seconds).
3. Verify lag in Grafana dashboard 'payments-consumer' drops below 1,000 messages within 5 minutes.
Rollback: none listed.
Escalation: none listed.
